needed: Township-level territorial control for September 2026, with per-township confidence and an as-of date, from IISS Myanmar Conflict Map and/or SAC-M.
why: The closing layer is deliberately limited to conservative state-level orientation. Control in an active war changes quickly, and converting a community reference image into precise front lines would imply evidence the project does not have.

needed: An independently reconciled constituency-level dataset for the 2025–26 military-run election, including cancellations, uncontested races and the areas where no voting occurred.
why: The current step reports official aggregate results and independently documented exclusions. Published accounts disagree on the exact township coverage, so the explainer does not present a single count as settled.

needed: A standardised cross-election table for 1990, 2015, 2020 and 2025–26, separating elected seats, appointed military seats, vacancies and contests across different levels of government.
why: Published figures differ depending on whether they count elected seats only, both chambers, or the full legislature including the reserved 25 per cent. A comparison across four elections is worthless unless the denominator is consistent.

needed: AAPP documented killings and detentions, each quoted with its as-of date.
why: AAPP figures rise continuously and are a verified floor, not a total. A number without a date implies a precision and a finality that the source does not claim.

needed: Internal displacement by state and refugee populations by destination country, from UN OCHA and UNHCR, with as-of dates.
why: The human layer of the final map depends on these. Round figures in general circulation are frequently out of date or conflate IDPs with refugees.

needed: Coordinates for Laiza, the KIO/KIA headquarters, from a citable gazetteer.
why: Laiza has no GeoNames entry. It is named in the narrative but carries no map pin, because an approximate pin on a headquarters location would look like a sourced fact.

needed: The full list of Nationwide Ceasefire Agreement signatories and non-signatories, including organisations that signed after October 2015.
why: The point of the signatory network visualisation is precisely who was in and who was out. Getting the membership approximately right would defeat it.

needed: A source-backed wind-field or damage-extent layer for Cyclone Nargis, separate from its NOAA best-track line.
why: The current animation uses selected NOAA IBTrACS positions and therefore shows direction and landfall only. It must not be read as the width of the storm or the boundary of damage.

needed: Which Karenni townships the Interim Executive Council administers, and which functions it delivers in each, from ISP-Myanmar or comparable field research.
why: The Karenni case study is meant to show what revolutionary government actually looks like in practice. Without township-level detail it becomes an assertion that it exists.
